collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — NATURE, ECOLOGY AND ANIMALS (NAT-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Isola's animals, plants, tides and weather: tide pools and nesting beaches, washed-up rubbish, shrinking clam beds, strange visitors, creatures doing what creatures do, and choices about the island where nobody gets a perfect answer.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A seabird is caught in a shiny line unlike any the village makes: untangle it together, or fetch someone who knows birds.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) finds a seabird on the rocks, flapping and stuck. A length of thin, clear fishing line, stiffer and shinier than any line the village makes, is wound around one leg and a wing. The more the bird struggles, the tighter it gets. It glares at (subject) with one furious yellow eye. (friend) comes running with a cloth.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) drops the cloth gently over the bird's head, and it goes still. (subject) works at the line with a sharp shell, a little at a time, while the bird grumbles under the cloth. It takes ages. At last the last loop falls away. They lift the cloth, step back, and the bird stands, shakes itself, and flies off, low and lopsided at first, then properly. (subject) keeps the line. (subject.He/she) has never seen anything like it, and (subject.he/she) doesn't want anything else to find it.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) stays with the bird while (friend) fetches (fisher), an old fisher who has freed more seabirds than anyone can count. (fisher) looks, sighs, and does it in a few quick, careful moves. The bird bites (fisher) on the thumb by way of thanks and flies off. "They always do that," says (fisher), sucking the thumb. "Every single time." The three of them spend the rest of the afternoon walking the rocks, picking up every scrap of that shiny line they can find.
